reviewed_version: Publisher version of record, DOI 10.1007/s00222-025-01397-y; publisher-hosted PDF with matching title, authors and DOI
inspection_outcome: Initial review completed with two Major and four Minor findings; delivery completion is separate from scientific adjudication.
summary: Printed preservation functional fails on translated ellipses and row-slot scaling gives a zero row in the claimed invertible limit. Concrete coordinated repairs, local formula corrections, positive proof checks and withdrawn circularity allegation are retained. Final geometric uniqueness statements are not disproved.

problems.title: Incompatible angular origins invalidate the preservation functional
problems.claim: Elliptic tangent weights annihilate printed caustic-preservation functionals and caustic-preserving graphs obey a quadratic bound.
problems.assumptions: Fixed sufficiently small positive e, a1, x-translation t->0, p1q3; all caustics remain, bounded C5/C39 norms and stated smallness threshold.
problems.check: Coordinate Jacobian yields mu_t=t bH2+O(t²); exact expansion gives integral(H2 c_printed)=pi e²/2+O(e4). Chord/support/reflection identities independently derive corrected action angle.
problems.result: Nonzero term linear in t contradicts printed O(t²) preservation estimate.
problems.impact: Core linearization and projection transfer fail as printed; no counterexample to final local rigidity theorem.
problems.correction: Use quarter-period-corrected F, physical cos-squared motion weights and corresponding Jcorr, both Fourier sectors; exact first variation restores tangent annihilation. Quantitative uniform q8 theorem must be carried through consistently.
problems.counterevidence: Changing scalar, phase or orientation does not annihilate a nonzero paired vector. Coherent paired rotations preserve finite rank, but the originally mixed full operator is not already conjugate.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: For r(phi)=(cos(phi),b sin(phi)), e^2=1−b^2, the boundary speed is v=sqrt(1−e^2 cos^2(phi)) and rho=v^3/b. Thus rho^(−2/3)ds is proportional to dphi/v, not the sin-squared density obtained from printed(2.7) at lambda0. The normal component of a horizontal translation gives mu_t=t b cos(phi)/(1−e^2 cos^2(phi))+O_C39(t^2). For p1q3, printed theta=phi−k^2 sin(2phi)/8+O(k^4), k^2=4e^2+O(e^4), and theta' cos(3theta)=cos(3phi)+(k^2/16)cos(phi)−(5k^2/16)cos(5phi)+O(k^4). Multiplying by H=cos(phi)+e^2(3cos(phi)+cos(3phi))/4+O(e^4) and integrating gives pi e^2/2+O(e^4), nonzero at fixed sufficiently small positive e. Hence the printed left side is linear in translation t, contradicting the quadratic right side of(7.1).
independent_acceptance.hypothesis_and_counterevidence_check: Translations preserve every elliptic caustic and have uniformly bounded C5/C39 graph norms for small t. Fixed q3 satisfies the displayed smallness threshold as t tends to0. Source(6.9)–(6.11) explicitly includes translations among valid motions, so an unstated centering restriction cannot remove this example. A scalar or paired sine/cosine phase rotation cannot make a nonzero paired coefficient vector vanish.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: The physical action angle is Theta=pi*[F(phi+pi/2,k)−K(k)]/[2K(k)]. The Jacobi chord/support identity with sn(v)=lambda/b and k^2=e^2/(1−lambda^2) yields the confocal tangent and reflection relation. The normal first variation is2lambda times the sum of mu over the polygon, so translated-ellipse perimeter invariance restores tangent annihilation with the coherent physical angle. The motion weights retain cos-squared denominators and Jcorr=(2K(e)/pi)sqrt(1−e^2 cos^2(phi)); paired Fourier rotations preserve the finite rank construction.
independent_acceptance.impact: The printed core preservation/projection chain fails. This is a counterexample to that intermediate claim, not to geometric rigidity of ellipses. Coherent finite changes do not prove that the originally mixed full operator was already conjugate, and the complete repaired uniform q^8 quantitative estimate remains to be supplied consistently.

problems.title: Row-slot index is incorrectly used in finite operator scaling
problems.claim: Scaled operator tends to a block matrix with invertible finite Ahat.
problems.assumptions: Allowed q0=3; selected positive rational rotations strictly below1/3; finite row n6 and all column frequencies3..q1.
problems.check: Each actual Q_n>3 but printed slot frequency3 gives O(e^(j-3+|Q_n-j|)), tending0 for every finite column.
problems.result: Entire finite row is zero in the claimed limit, independently of coordinate defect.
problems.impact: Invalidates stated near-circle invertibility input to analytic Fredholm and nonlinear argument; final theorem not disproved.
problems.correction: Replace left power by e^(q1-Q_n), preserving actual caustic constants and right power. Check bounded left factors, vanishing C, unchanged B, square-summable D-I. Normalize constant motion row separately.
problems.counterevidence: No relabeling creates missing denominator3; finite prefactors do not correct exponent. Algebraic finite matrices remain nondegenerate after proper scaling.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: Lemma4.1 permits q0=3 and selects positive p_n/q_n<1/3, so every actual q_n>3. The first nonelliptic row has slot n6, giving floor(n/2)=3 in(6.26), although its true denominator is q_n. Multiplication by the right factor gives e^(j−3)A_(p_n,q_n,j). Every finite column j3..q1 is O(e^(j−3+|q_n−j|)), which tends to0: if j<=q_n the exponent is q_n−3>0, otherwise it is2j−q_n−3>0. Opposite parity entries vanish. Thus the entire row of the claimed limiting finite block is zero, contradicting its asserted invertibility.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: This remains a defect when the abstract Fourier coefficients are treated separately from P1. Source(6.11) attaches selected caustics to slots, while(4.1)/(4.33) use actual denominators; a relabeling or finite nonzero prefactor cannot manufacture denominator3. The algebraic nondegenerate finite matrices themselves are not refuted.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: Use actual left exponent e^(q1−q_n) and the unchanged column exponent e^(j−q1), with the finite caustic constants from the correct odd/even scaling. Since q_n<=q1, left factors are bounded. The finite-to-high block C tends to0, the high-to-finite B retains its geometric-tail control, and the D−Id estimate remains square summable. The constant mode has h1(0)=1 versus the normalized Fourier constant1/sqrt(2pi), giving a harmless separate sqrt(2) diagonal normalization rather than the printed identity.
independent_acceptance.impact: The incorrect near-circle operator limit is an essential input to the analytic-Fredholm/nonlinear route. A coordinated repair is available at the block level; the original limit is still invalid and no final-theorem counterexample follows.

problems.title: Exact sine and cosine coefficient families differ
problems.claim: The two unmixed Fourier coefficient families agree exactly.
problems.assumptions: p1,qj3; elliptic nome expansion with paired Fourier symmetries.
problems.check: Direct convolution gives E_(q-j)/2 plus/minus E_-(q+j)/2; difference -2nu³+O(nu5).
problems.impact: Separate exact families needed; common leading matrices and finite-rank proof survive.
problems.correction: Retain both branches; use common leading asymptotics only. Generating function gives general binomial coefficients.
problems.counterevidence: Mixed-parity vanishing is valid but does not equate unmixed entries; opposite-frequency term starts at least two orders above leading.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: Writing E=exp_*(j w) for the bilateral nome coefficients gives A_plus=E_((q−j)/2)+E_(−(q+j)/2), while A_minus has a minus before the second term. For q=j3 the latter coefficient begins −nu^3+O(nu^5), so A_plus−A_minus=−2nu^3+O(nu^5), not zero. The exact leading bilateral generating functions (1−nu z)^(−j)(1−nu z^(−1))^j independently supply this sign and coefficient.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_repair: Parity vanishing does not identify the two unmixed sectors. The opposite-frequency contribution is min(q,j)>=2 nome orders above the leading term, so their leading coefficient matrices agree even though the exact families differ. Keep both branches and use common leading asymptotics only; the finite-rank argument survives.
independent_acceptance.execution_scope: The algebraic expansion was independently checked symbolically in reasoning. Historical saved exact/numerical diagnostics were not re-executed and are not represented as new computations.

problems.title: Uniform asymptotic bound requires a rotation ceiling
problems.claim: One absolute constant controls advertised p/q<1/2 coefficient bound.
problems.assumptions: Interpretation as uniform absolute C; coprime j3,q2y+3,p(q-1)/2; take e->0 for each fixed pair then y->infinity.
problems.result: Absolute bound over whole rotation range fails; pair-dependent interpretation needs explicit statement.
problems.impact: Local uniformity gap; main construction may use stricter cutoff and fixed ceiling.
problems.correction: Require p/q<=omega_max<1/2 with C and small-e threshold depending on ceiling.
problems.counterevidence: If some constant means pair-dependent, no contradiction for fixed pair; that reading supplies no absolute uniform bound. Actual p1 tail has a fixed ceiling.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: On an absolute-uniform reading of(1.6), set j3, q=2y+3, p=(q−1)/2; the last two are coprime and p/q<1/2. For each fixed pair first take e->0. The leading coefficient is B_y=binom(y+2,2)/(16^y sin^(2y)(pi/(2q))) >= binom(y+2,2)*(q^2/(4pi^2))^y. It cannot be bounded by one C^(3y+4) as y->infinity. A pair-dependent small-e threshold does not remove this leading-coefficient obstruction to an absolute C.
independent_acceptance.quantifier_qualification: The literal phrase 'some constant C' is ambiguous. If C is allowed to depend on the fixed pair, this is not a contradiction for that pair, and no unconditional false-theorem claim is made. The proof's comparison k_(p/q)<k_(1/3) and its stated pursuit of uniform bounds nevertheless require a restricted rotation range.
independent_acceptance.repair_and_impact: State p/q<=omega_max<1/2 and allow C and the small-e threshold to depend on that ceiling. The main construction may increase q0 and its p1 tail has a fixed ceiling, so this is a local uniformity/exposition defect and not evidence that the main theorem fails.

problems.title: Printed lower spectral-separation bound contradicts strict chord length
problems.claim: t_pq >= (2p-1)ell/p for all relevant large periods.
problems.assumptions: Smooth strictly convex ellipse; p1 and arbitrarily large rational q.
problems.check: Strict chord-versus-boundary-arc comparison gives every one-winding polygon length<ell.
problems.result: Contradiction for p1 for every finite q; increasing q0 does not cure literal formula.
problems.impact: Local separation formula needs repair; intended exclusion of perimeter multiples survives.
problems.correction: Use (p-1/2)ell<t<=T<pell for bounded numerators after increasing q0 via existing asymptotics.
problems.counterevidence: Numerical examples illustrate but strict geometric inequality proves contradiction. Corrected bound also excludes intermediate multiples for p>=3.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: For a strictly convex ellipse, each finite one-winding inscribed polygon has every chord strictly shorter than its corresponding positive boundary arc, hence T_(1,q)<ell for every finite q. Arbitrarily large rational-caustic periods exist. Substituting p1 in the printed(8.52) gives t_(1,q)>=ell, contradicting that strict inequality regardless of q0.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: For bounded1<=p<=7, the actual uniform expansion(8.33) gives t_(p,q)=p ell−c_(2,p)q^(−2)+O(q^(−4)); the coefficient and remainder are bounded in the stated near-ellipse family and ell has a positive lower bound. Increasing q0 therefore yields (p−1/2)ell=3.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence_and_impact: The decisive evidence is geometric and exact. Historical floating-point deficits merely illustrate it and were not newly rerun or upgraded to interval certificates. The corrected separation gives the intended use, so the local formula is Minor.

problems.title: Reciprocal normalization in spectral-coefficient identification
problems.claim: Printed reciprocal map sends ellipse tail to integers and yields stated ratio.
problems.assumptions: c0,c>0, common perimeter and near-ellipse smallness; endpoints visible on every sufficiently large q.
problems.check: Printed g yields q/c0. Correct g=sqrt(c0)/sqrt(x), ratio sqrt(c0/c); own-coefficient interval and integer-gap proof handles weaker remainder.
problems.result: Two reciprocal factors incorrect; noncircular corrected argument establishes coefficient equality.
problems.impact: Local formulas and proof exposition need correction; coefficient-identification conclusion preserved.
problems.correction: Use each domain's own coefficient to isolate visible intervals first; |n(q)-lambda q|<=Cepsilon+C'/q, every large-q integer gap1, then lambda1.
problems.counterevidence: Potential Major circularity allegation withdrawn: author says follow ideas and distinguishes coefficients. Endpoint visibility before equality and positive separation polynomial provide explicit repair.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: Let c0=c_(2,1)(E) and c=c_(2,1)(Omega)>0. The printed map c0^(−1/2)x^(−1/2), applied at x=c0 q^(−2)+O(q^(−4)), gives q/c0+O(1/q), not q+O(1/q). The corrected map is sqrt(c0)x^(−1/2), and deformed tails have scaling lambda=sqrt(c0/c), the reciprocal of(8.61).
independent_acceptance.noncircular_repair: Before identifying c with c0, use each domain's own coefficient to isolate its large-q intervals near the common perimeter. The exact adjacent-interval separation numerator after multiplying by10q^3(q+1)^3 is18q^3+27q^2+7q−1>0. Other winding types are excluded by large-p bounds, bounded-p asymptotics and continuity for finitely many remaining types. Lemma8.8 then gives a visible endpoint for every sufficiently large integer q before coefficient equality. Spectral matching yields integers n(q) with |n(q)−lambda q|<=C epsilon+C'/q. Choose the uniform error eta<1/5 and |lambda−1|<1/10; then |n(q+1)−n(q)−1|<2eta+1/10<1/2, so every sufficiently large gap is1. Consequently n(q)=q+d and lambda=1.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The source explicitly says to follow the ideas of preceding lemmas and distinguishes the coefficients. That permits the own-coefficient reconstruction; it does not justify retaining a categorical Major circularity allegation. Requiring visible endpoints for all large q is essential; an unspecified subsequence would not suffice.
independent_acceptance.impact_and_scope: The reciprocal formulas need correction but the coefficient equality can be recovered. For full isospectrality, the common perimeter is a heat invariant; for the germ claim the nearby unique accumulation point requires its stated local interpretation. The external endpoint-visibility microlocal input is not newly reproved in full.
